title: Billy Cobham - Wikipedia
notes: Born in Colón, Panama; drums from four, with his father at eight; Music & Art High School; Army band 1965-68; Horace Silver; Miles Davis (A Tribute to Jack Johnson, Big Fun, Live-Evil, Get Up with It); the Mahavishnu Orchestra (1971-73); Spectrum No. 1 on the jazz chart; open-handed; his 1970s kit; the drummers he cites; Collins on The Inner Mounting Flame; halls of fame. No Headhunters credit.

title: Spectrum (Billy Cobham album) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded 14-16 May 1973. Tommy Bolin and Lee Sklar on Quadrant 4, Taurian Matador, Stratus and Red Baron; Ron Carter, Joe Farrell, Jimmy Owens and Ray Barretto on Spectrum; Cobham does not play on To the Women in My Life. Stratus is the sample in Massive Attack's Safe from Harm.

title: Todd Bishop, Let's talk about Billy Cobham (cruiseshipdrummer.com, 2020)
notes: 'Snare drummy'; 'the first major player to play the drums open handed'; singles and open rolls with accented singles; 'an energy sound, not a deep power sound'; a tight, dry, high snare; the china mounted upside down.

title: Todd Bishop, Groove o' the day: Billy Cobham - White Rabbit
notes: Three phases: the flamenco beat (hat foot on 2 and 4), the funk beat, and the bell of the ride accenting the "and"s.

title: Todd Bishop, Groove o' the day: Billy Cobham in 7/8
notes: Spectrum: unaccented notes played strong, a light accent on the last note of a sixteenth triplet, sticking LRL.

title: Joe Bergamini, COBHAM: The Music and Drumming of Billy Cobham (Hudson Music)
notes: Not read: its contents (Right Off, Quadrant 4, Stratus, Spectrum, Red Baron, Spanish Moss, Heather, Solarization) and the double-bass shuffle of Quadrant 4 are from a search summary.

title: White Rabbit (George Benson album) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded November 1971 at Van Gelder Studio; Cobham on drums (search summary).
